sentences.text: Koshisaurus was distinct from most hadrosauroids because it possessed an antorbital fossa and three ridges on its upper teeth.
This single-species genus was found in the Kitadani Formation of Japan, where 'Koshi' is an old regional name for the area in Fukui prefecture.
Other Asian genera like Xuwulong, Jinzhousaurus, and Altirhinus share the tooth ridges but lack the antorbital fossa, making them more evolutionarily advanced than Koshisaurus.
Koshisaurus belongs to the superfamily Hadrosauroidea, and its discovery suggests that hadrosauroids were more diverse along the eastern edge of Asia during the Early Cretaceous.

The animal lived in what is now Asia during the middle of the Cretaceous period, approximately 128 million years ago in the Aptian age, with a time range estimated between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
